subject: Dark mode: follow the OS, honor the theming setting, dark title bars
body:
Dark mode: follow the OS, honor the theming setting, dark title bars

mRemoteNG already shipped three dark themes, but they did not read as dark
and were hard to reach. Close the gaps rather than add another theme.

ThemeManager hardcoded _themeActive = true and never read the persisted
ThemingActive setting, so the documented 'themes are off by default' was
untrue and the setting was inert. Honor it, and flip its default to True so
honoring it does not silently turn theming off for everyone (ActiveTheme
falls back to the light DefaultTheme whenever theming is inactive).

Add FollowOsTheme (default on): at startup, match the Windows app mode by
reading AppsUseLightTheme and select OsDarkThemeName/OsLightThemeName. This
is resolved at startup only. DockPanelSuite's ThemeBase.ApplyTo throws if
the DockPanel holds any pane, float window or content, so re-theming a
running instance would mean closing every open connection.

Dark the window title bars via DWMWA_USE_IMMERSIVE_DARK_MODE. The caption is
drawn by the shell, so no palette entry can reach it, and a light caption was
the most visible tell that dark mode was not really on. Theme darkness is
decided by measuring the palette's own dialog background rather than matching
theme names, so cloned and hand-edited themes classify correctly.

Theme the Options dialog. Its ApplyTheme call and ThemeChanged subscription
were commented out, leaving light chrome framing pages that already theme
themselves. FrmMain.RecreateOptionsForm disposes and rebuilds the form, so a
stale subscription could fire on a disposed form -- the likely reason it was
disabled. Guard against that and unsubscribe on close.

Add a 'Match the Windows app theme' checkbox to the Theme options page, which
disables the theme list while active, since an explicit pick and OS following
are mutually exclusive.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

triage.rationale: Follow-OS dark mode + DWM dark title bars addresses open #47. Clean idea, but flips ThemingActive default and our ThemeManager/settings diverged; re-derive carefully.

votes.concern: Default-on OS following silently overrides and persists over existing users’ explicit or custom theme selections.
votes.reason: OS matching is valuable, but this untested patch conflicts with live-switch and high-contrast theming, assumes restart-only behavior, and requires a scoped reimplementation.

votes.concern: Upgraded user profiles with saved ThemingActive=False will have theming disabled, and settings files are prone to designer merge conflicts.
votes.reason: Valuable dark mode UX improvements matching modern Windows settings, but requires careful refactoring of settings and ThemeManager initialization to prevent regressions.

dissent: codex: REJECT - OS matching is valuable, but this untested patch conflicts with live-switch and high-contrast theming, assumes restart-only behavior, and requires a scoped reimplementation.
